findings.text: Ask 3 is not done: `Server/Unclose.mjs --apply` was never run (no `public/framework/ai/unclose-manifest.jsonl` exists), and `census.md` is a byte-for-byte copy of `census-before.md` (same 20:41Z stamp, `abandoned 459`, no `unclosed`). Run the apply after the merge, rerun the census, and put the before and after numbers in the outcome.

`Server/doc/stale-close.md` (new "Unclosed" section, last sentence) says "On 2026-11-02 it was applied in the main tree after the merge". That has not happened yet, so the doc states something false. Write the sentence after the apply, with the real count.

Commit-triggered completion will close multi-turn agents' tasks too early. `Servex/CloseLoop.js:393` treats any `commit` line as "finished", and `Agents.js` `close_loop()` runs for every role at every idle turn end. CLAUDE.md says to commit after every working step, and this task's own `session.jsonl` already has a commit line (`3c29ade4df8d`). So a mastermind that commits, then ends its turn while it waits for `review.mjs`, a background shell or the owner, gets its task completed from its last words. The readme's "Caveat" bullet admits this but doesn't prevent it. Narrow it: for masterminds, count only an outcome or landing line as finished, and let a commit count only for minions.

The `census.mjs` copy prints no `unclosed` column (lines 62–64: the per-day and by-creator tables list landed, stalled, abandoned, stopped and open only). Even after the apply, the markdown would not show the new state, so the before and after numbers can't be read from it. A second copy of `../task-system-audit/census.mjs` also goes against "one of everything": extend the original instead.

`core/Task/readme.md:89` is now stale. It still says StaleClose "appends a `stop` line … to every `stale` task", but worked tasks now get `{"unclosed":…}`. Also, ask 5 put `unclosed` under "Watch out" rather than with the task states ("Replay, waiting, subtasks", lines 54–58, where `stopped` and `waiting` are defined).

A fresh agent could not continue from this folder. `session.jsonl` has the assign, one edit and one commit: no log lines, no outcome, and no record that the apply, the census rerun, the merge and the Servex restart are still owed. Ask 3 and the brief's "say a restart is needed" have no record anywhere in the task.

`StaleClose.worked` (`Server/StaleClose.mjs`, `WORKED = 3`) counts the launcher's own `assign` and `start` lines. So a single log line makes a task "real work" (the test at `Server/Unclose.test.mjs:303` confirms it), and the 224-task figure may grow to include near-empty tasks. Counting lines other than assign and start would be closer to "224 had real work".

`.claude/hooks/jsonl-schema.mjs:12`: `wait:` lost a space of alignment. `Server/PromptAudit-stream.test.mjs:97–98` builds an empty file through a pointless `jl()` helper; `fs.writeFileSync(f, "")` says the same thing.

The tests stub the agent and host rather than using the TestRunner fence. That fence (`Server/ServexFence.mjs`) is Playwright-only, so the stubs are the right call: none of these tests touch the live Servex. All five pass in the worktree: close-loop, Unclose (16), PromptAudit-stream, AIIndex, and stale-close (15).

Ask 2 is met: `PromptAudit.each_line` streams in 8 MB chunks, cuts lines at a newline byte, and has a test. The `--days 7` output is saved (`prompt-audit-days7.txt`, empty `.err`). It reports only 1 session and 104 prompts for the week, which is worth a glance to make sure it's real.

findings.text: Nothing in the task folder says why this second round exists. `requirements.md` has no ask for "news does not wake a landed worker", and `session.jsonl` ends with commit `d2af39b4c90e` but has no log line naming the ask, its source or what it adds. A fresh agent could not tell whether `worktree/task-close-loop-2` is in scope. Add a log line that links the source of the ask, or add it to the brief as ask 6.

The task still has no outcome. The apply has run (`public/framework/ai/unclose-manifest.jsonl`, 390 lines) and `census.md` was recomputed at 21:01Z (all-time: unclosed 383, abandoned 76; before: abandoned 459). But `session.jsonl` has no `complete` line, and no log line saying the owed steps 2–3 from the 14:56 log line are done. Ask 3 wants the before and after numbers in the outcome, and the brief wants "a Servex restart is needed" said in the report.

A diverted message looks delivered. `Servex/agents/Agents.js:1525`: `landed_fyi` returns `this` from `send()`, so `send_to_agent` (`Servex/agents/tools.js:481-492`) gives the sender the agent card as if the message arrived. A sibling that asked a question with `reply_to` then waits for an answer that never comes. The same situation for a dormant landed agent already throws "was not woken: its task … has landed. Pass revive: true" (`Agents.js:661-664`, `blocked()`). Tell the sender the same way, e.g. a `{held: "fyi"}` marker that `send_to_agent` reports.

There is a simpler way, and it keeps one system (law 6). `landed_fyi` repeats the landed check that `blocked()` (`Agents.js:684-692`) and `watchdog_refusal` (`Agents.js:1729`) already make, and it adds a third exemption list (`WAKES_LANDED`, plus a mastermind role regex) beside the `STANDING` regex at `Agents.js:1217`. Folding the rule into `blocked()`/`watchdog_refusal` with one sender allow-list would keep the "who may wake a landed agent" rule in one place.

`WAKES_LANDED` (`Agents.js:1728`) also matches `user…` senders, but the readme bullet (`Servex/agents/readme.md:78`) lists only the owner, `vscode-`, `voice` and `tab-`. Name `user` there too, or drop it.
The re-close touched 383 tasks, not the brief's 224. That is expected after review finding 7 changed `StaleClose.worked`, but the outcome should give that reason so nobody reads it as a miscount.

The tests pass: `node Servex/agents/close-loop.test.mjs` prints `ok` in the `task-close-loop-2` worktree. Case 5 covers each sender exemption, the mastermind exemption, an open task, and `send()` not pushing. The new code needs the same Servex restart as round 1, and the report should say so.

findings.text: The diff does not touch requirements.md at all: it only changes the `Task.completion` formula (Task.js:316), and none of asks 1-5 (the close loop, PromptAudit streaming, the unclosed re-close script, the tests, the docs) appear in it. They landed earlier in 3c29ade4d and 6fdafebb8 (`git log`), so the task folder should say which commit holds which ask and that this diff is a separate owner ask (2026-11-02, the average-of-completions formula); as it stands a fresh agent cannot tell what this diff belongs to.

`core/Session/readme.md` is updated at line 23 in the diff, but `core/doc/overview.md:149` (`progress()  // done / total of the subtasks`) is not. It is still accurate for `progress()`, so it needs no change. `core/Task/Prompt.js:125-127` falls back to `done / total` for `Prompt.completion` when it has no parts, so a Prompt's completion ignores the half-done rule while every other Task uses it. Either apply the same average there or state the exception in `core/Task/readme.md` next to line 98.

`ai/AISession/SessionStats.js:42` still says "Root tasks done ÷ total" next to `Session.completion`. The count line it feeds ("N of M tasks done") is still true, but a reader will expect the session percentage to equal done/total, and it no longer does (the test now expects 0.875 for 3 of 4). Add one line saying the percentage is the average of the tasks' own completions.

Task.js:66-67 has the right shape: it recurses, leaves stopped tasks out, and the new check in Task.test.mjs covers a half-done subtask and a stopped one. The inline `typeof t.completion === "number"` guard is probably dead code, because every Task has the getter. It can go if nothing relies on non-Task children.

The comment at Task.js:60 and the readme both say "the one computed form", which is now two code paths: `progress_of` (counts) and the average. That is fine as long as `progress()` stays the counts; the comment above `progress_of` (Task.js:168-171) should say it is for counts only, not for completion.
Simpler way: none better. A subtask average that recurses is the shortest way to give the owner's formula, and nothing is stored.

Because completion now recurses, a complete parent with open children (state complete, completion under 1) reads below 1 unless `checked_by` is set. That was true before for one level, but it now shows at depth too; worth a line in the Task readme under "completion" if sessions are expected to reach 100% only when every nested task is closed.
